steps.title: Greek seafood
steps.body: Dry Assyrtiko suits Greek food: grilled octopus, sea bass, shellfish, fava, Santorini's yellow split pea purée, tomato fritters and feta. Its acidity cuts through olive oil and fried food. Its saline edge suits oysters and sushi too.

steps.title: Service and age
steps.body: Serve dry Assyrtiko at 8 to 11 degrees. It ages surprisingly well thanks to its acidity: top Santorini wines develop over 10 to 15 years, gaining smoky, honeyed notes. Vinsanto, served at 12 to 14, suits dried fruit, nuts, blue cheese and chocolate.

steps.explanation: Its acidity and salinity suit grilled seafood.

steps.body: Fava, Santorini's yellow split pea purée with olive oil and onions, is a local classic with Assyrtiko.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Dry Assyrtiko suits grilled octopus, fava and seafood
Top Santorini Assyrtiko ages 10 to 15 years
Vinsanto suits dried fruit, cheese and chocolate
